title: The Nalanda Pupils Who Dug Wells in an Outcaste Village
conflicts: Participants: 75 teachers and students (1969 Magsaysay citation) vs 40 students and 12 teachers (NYT obituary 2024, Bond 2003) vs about forty students (AsiaNews); story gives both main figures with sources. Work done: wells, latrines, gardens, starting/repairing the school (Magsaysay, NYT) vs building a road (Tricycle); story names the agreed work and mentions the road. Birth year 1931 (NYT, Sarvodaya, Daily Mirror) vs 1932 (Tricycle); 1931 used. A 2009 Sunday Observer letter reportedly credits the Department of Rural Development with organising the camp; the page is 403 and unread, so the story says Ariyaratne led the Nalanda party rather than organised the whole camp.
notes: No first-person Ariyaratne account of the camp could be found on a page that loads; his reasoning comes from the 1969 Magsaysay biography and his own words from his Magsaysay response speech. His son's Berkley Center interview supports the detail that he kept teaching until 1972.
